policy_prompt_for_subgoal: The goal instruction names how many cubes of which color(s) must go into the bin before the button is pressed (e.g. 'two blue cubes' or 'one red cube and three green cubes'). Apply these rules at every decision step, using the scene shown and the memory field `placed` as updated at this step. Rule 1 (holding): If the scene at this decision step shows a cube 'held in the gripper', choose B: put it into the bin. This holds whatever `placed` contains. Rule 2 (done): If no cube is held and, for every color named in the goal, the number of entries of that color in `placed` is at least the number the goal asks for, choose C: press the button. The episode ends there. Rule 3 (pick): If no cube is held and some goal color still has fewer entries in `placed` than required, choose A: pick up the cube, pointing at a cube of a color that is still needed. Where two colors are still needed, choose the color this way: if `placed` is non-empty and its last entry is a color that still has fewer entries in `placed` than the goal requires, pick that same color again (a color once started is finished before any other color is touched); only when the last-placed color is complete move to another needed color. If `placed` is empty, any needed color may be started; as the fixed default, start the needed color with the larger required count, ties to the color named first in the goal instruction. Among the cubes of that color, pick the oldest one on the table: point at the position of the first entry in `cubes` (as updated at this step) that has that color. If the scene at this decision step shows a detection of that color within about 10 px of that entry, point at that detection's center; if not (the arm may be covering it), point at the remembered position. Do not discard a detection for drifting by a few pixels between frames, and never point at a detection lying on top of the bin's position. At step #1 the first entry of `cubes` is the needed-color cube nearest the bin's center. A point offset by a pixel or two from the detection center is acceptable; cubes of other colors are distractors and are never picked. Never point at the bin or the button. An episode starts in A at step #1: the gripper is raised out of the frame, `placed` is empty, so pick up a cube of a needed color. If a situation matches none of the rules (for example the fingers are closed but no cube is reported held, or no cube of a needed color is visible): if the fingers are partly closed treat it as holding and choose B; otherwise choose A pointing at the first entry of `cubes` whose color is still needed, and if `cubes` has no such entry, choose A pointing at any visible cube of a needed color, or failing that any visible cube. Never choose C unless Rule 2 is satisfied.

fields.name: placed
fields.description: Ordered list of the colors of the cubes that have been put into the bin so far, oldest first. When the carried-in memory is blank (the first decision step), write placed=[] explicitly: the field is always output as an explicit list, even when empty. Copy the carried-in list unchanged, except: if the execution steps shown at this step contain a frame with a cube 'held in the gripper' and the scene at this decision step shows the gripper open (about 100%) with no cube held, then the robot has just released a cube into the bin, so append that held cube's color once. Do not append when the step ends with a cube still held (that was a pick-up), when there are no execution steps (first step), or when the robot only pressed the button. Ignore cubes that appear or vanish on the table; only the held-then-released event counts. Write the list as a JSON array with double-quoted strings, never Python-style single quotes; the field is compared literally. e.g. ["green", "green"]

fields.name: cubes
fields.description: Ordered list of the cubes of the goal colors on the table and not yet picked, oldest first, each as [color, [y, x]]. When the carried-in memory is blank (the first decision step), list every visible cube of a goal color ordered by distance to the bin's center, nearest first (ties: smaller y). Otherwise copy the carried-in list and: remove the entry nearest (within about 10 px) the place where the execution steps show the gripper closing on and lifting a cube; append, in order of first appearance, each cube of a goal color that shows up during the execution steps at a place where no entry lies within about 10 px (ignore detections at the bin's position and the 'held in the gripper' detection; a cube that vanishes for a frame or two because the arm covers it keeps its entry, do not re-add it); refresh each entry's position to the latest place it was reported. Never reorder entries: the list order is the age order and nothing seen later changes it. Cubes of colors not named in the goal are never entered. Write it as a JSON array with double-quoted color strings. e.g. [["blue", [54, 118]], ["blue", [87, 181]]]
